title: Everguard Insurance - Private VPC discovery
summary: Discovery focused on Everguard's requirements for a private VPC deployment of Redwood Private. Key concerns: cross-account peering vs PrivateLink, region constraints (EU residency), CIDR overlap, KMS/BYOK, SOC2/audit logs, and pilot timeline. AE + SE to share security pack, network diagram template, and pricing. Follow-up to schedule network deep-dive with cloud infra team and security.
next_steps: Alex Kim: Send security whitepaper + SOC2 docs by 2026-05-10
Priya Sharma: Share network diagram template and example PrivateLink architecture by 2026-05-12
Schedule technical deep-dive with Everguard infra (Ethan + Samuel) for week of 2026-05-18
Provide rough sizing/pricing for Dedicated vs Private options
action_items: Alex Kim; Send security whitepaper and SOC2 report; due 2026-05-10
Priya Sharma; Prepare network diagram + sample CloudFormation snippets for PrivateLink and Transit Gateway; due 2026-05-12
Ethan Ross; Share current VPC CIDR ranges and region list; due 2026-05-11
transcript:
Meeting: Everguard Insurance - Private VPC discovery
Date: 2026-05-07
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (CTO), Ethan Ross (Infra), Samuel Price (Security)

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Priya our SE, say hi Priya.
[00:06] Priya Sharma: hey hi, thanks for having us, excited to walk through your network and see how Redwood Private might fit.
[00:12] Maya Lopez: great thanks Alex, we've got about 45 minutes, we'll start with a quick overview of what we have and then go into networking questions.
[00:20] Ethan Ross: yep i'll try to keep it focused, we run mostly in AWS, two primary orgs for EU and NA, and our infra team manages VPCs across accounts.
[00:28] Samuel Price: and from security I'll ask about KMS, logs, and access controls. we do have strict residency requirements for EU customers.
[00:36] Alex Kim: perfect, the agenda i sent was: quick product fit, networking options (peering vs privatelink), security integrations (BYOK/KMS, audit logs), and next steps. any additions?
[00:45] Maya Lopez: nope that's good. one ask up front: we can't send traffic over the public internet for inference calls for EU PII. so Private VPC or VPC peering is a must.
[00:56] Priya Sharma: understood. Redwood Private supports a few deployment patterns: cross-account VPC peering, Transit Gateway peering, and PrivateLink (interface endpoints). each has tradeoffs around routing, IP management, and scalability.
[01:10] Ethan Ross: can you clarify PrivateLink vs peering? we have overlapping /16 ranges in some accounts, peering might be messy.
[01:20] Priya Sharma: yeah so peering requires non-overlapping CIDRs. if you have overlap, PrivateLink (AWS NLB + interface endpoints) avoids that by using ENIs in your VPC and a private endpoint. it's more work to set up but isolates routing.
[01:32] Alex Kim: to add, Transit Gateway can centralize routing and attach multiple VPCs, which helps if you want to expose Redwood Private to many accounts without tons of pairings.
[01:40] Ethan Ross: we use TGW in NA but not in EU yet. for EU we prefer direct peering or endpoints because TGW adds cost.
[01:48] Samuel Price: what about cross-region? our EU data must remain in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1, can't route to us-east-1.
[01:56] Priya Sharma: Redwood Private can be deployed in a single region VPC controlled by the customer; we can map model serving region-by-region. for EU residency we'd provision in eu-west-1 and ensure no cross-region egress for those requests. we also support region pinning.
[02:10] Maya Lopez: good. is there a managed component from Redwood inside our VPC or do you operate in your account?
[02:18] Alex Kim: there are two common patterns: 1) customer-managed VPC where Redwood Private runs in your account (we supply AMIs/helm charts for on-prem/k8s) or 2) a customer VPC peering to Redwood-managed VPCs for hosted-ish deployments. For full control and compliance, most enterprise customers prefer customer-controlled VPCs.
[02:36] Ethan Ross: if we go customer-managed, how does updates/rollouts work? we need canary and rollback.
[02:42] Priya Sharma: the control plane can be run privately; we push images and you control the runtime. we support canary rollouts and health checks; the orchestration is designed so you can approve upgrades. sometimes transcription says "control plane" weirdly but in practice we can do offline approvals.
[02:59] Samuel Price: KMS - can we use our own CMKs with HSM/CloudHSM? encryption at rest is required.
[03:06] Priya Sharma: yes BYOK is supported. Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS (AWS KMS) and can be configured to use your CMKs. for HSM-backed keys we typically integrate via CloudHSM + KMS.
[03:16] Maya Lopez: audit trails. how granular are logs? we need per-request audit logs for regulatory review, and retention for 7 years for some products.
[03:26] Alex Kim: we can send audit logs to your S3 or to your SIEM via Kinesis/Firehose. logs include request metadata, timestamps, and model versioning. retention policies are customer-managed.
[03:35] Ethan Ross: network nitty gritty - what ports and IP ranges do we need to open? any requirement for NAT?
[03:43] Priya Sharma: if you use PrivateLink, you create interface endpoints which use elastic network interfaces and security groups. For peering/Transit Gateway, you need to ensure route tables send traffic to Redwood subnets and security groups allow inbound from your service subnets on the ports we specify (usually gRPC/HTTPS 443 and internal ports for health). We provide a network checklist.
[04:02] Maya Lopez: is there an option for TLS termination inside our VPC? we prefer to terminate on our side and maintain mTLS to the service.
[04:09] Priya Sharma: yes mTLS is supported; we can provide mutual TLS between your service and the model runtime. certs can be managed via your PKI.
[04:16] Samuel Price: SSO integration - SAML/SSO for audit and RBAC.
[04:20] Alex Kim: Redwood Console supports SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync; RBAC at the token and project level. for Private deployments, you can run the control plane behind your SSO provider.
[04:29] Ethan Ross: what's the typical latency impact of PrivateLink vs peering? we have strict latency SLOs for real-time inferencing.
[04:36] Priya Sharma: PrivateLink adds a small hop but it's still over AWS backbone; for most workloads we see single-digit ms additional latency. Peering is slightly lower latency but requires non-overlapping CIDRs and can be heavier to manage at scale. We'll share benchmark numbers.
[04:52] Maya Lopez: cost - how does billing work for private deployments? we need cost predictability.
[04:57] Alex Kim: there are a few parts: infra cost (your VPC, NLBs, TGW), Redwood software license (platform fee for Private), and optional support/SLA. For Dedicated we offer reserved capacity pricing. We'll provide a rough TCO vs hosted.
[05:10] Ethan Ross: about IP ranges again - we have overlapping /24s with some subsidiaries, and can't renumber easily. looks like PrivateLink is our only immediate option.
[05:18] Priya Sharma: understood. PrivateLink will work with overlapping ranges. we'll include sample CloudFormation/terraform to provision interface endpoints and NLBs to present the service.
[05:28] Samuel Price: what about incident response? if there is a data exfil attempt, we want ability to revoke access and see all API keys and tokens usage.
[05:36] Alex Kim: audit logs + token-level tracing are available. you can revoke API keys and rotate them; for Private we recommend putting control plane access behind SSO and issuing short-lived tokens.
[05:47] Maya Lopez: any limitations around model sizes or GPU placement in Private? some of our batch jobs need larger GPUs.
[05:55] Priya Sharma: you can configure node types in your cluster; we support GPUs and can recommend instance types. for very large models we may suggest multi-GPU nodes and specific kernel optimizations.
[06:07] Ethan Ross: what's the onboarding timeline for a pilot? we'd like to run a small pilot on eu-west-1 with one model and a small baseline load.
[06:13] Alex Kim: typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: network setup (1 week), deploy runtime & test (1 week), run samples and tune (1 week). with your input we can tighten this.
[06:23] Maya Lopez: for procurement we need a security questionnaire answered and SOC2 Type II evidence.
[06:29] Alex Kim: we'll send the security pack and attestations. expect SOC2, ISO, and a sys design doc in the package.
[06:36] Ethan Ross: can we see a sample network diagram for PrivateLink + TGW so we can present to our architects?
[06:43] Priya Sharma: yes, i'll share a diagram and a template terraform/CFN by next week.
[06:50] Samuel Price: question: do you support bringing your own HSM cluster on-prem and having Redwood use it, or must it be cloud KMS?
[06:59] Priya Sharma: we integrate with cloud KMS primarily. for on-prem HSMs we can work via a proxy pattern but that usually requires an engineering engagement. we can discuss during the technical deep-dive.
[07:12] Alex Kim: quick note on fallbacks - if capacity is constrained in EU, policies can be set to fail closed or degrade to a smaller model in-region. we do not route EU PII to US unless explicitly configured.
[07:25] Maya Lopez: excellent. one red flag internally will be any chance of model logs leaving region. confirm logs can be stored in our S3 bucket in eu-west-1 only.
[07:34] Priya Sharma: yes logs can be exported to your S3 in-region only. we also support putting logs behind Kinesis with encryption.
[07:41] Ethan Ross: about network ports again, do you require opening 22 for updates? we prefer agentless approaches.
[07:47] Priya Sharma: we use secure image-based deploys and don't require SSH into your hosts; updates are done via orchestrator and container images.
[07:55] Maya Lopez: what's the minimum resource footprint to run a small pilot - like 2 vCPU nodes or more?
[08:00] Priya Sharma: for a small latency-sensitive model we'd recommend at least one GPU-backed instance; for CPU-only evals 2x m5.large-type nodes could work. we'll size based on model and QPS.
[08:10] Alex Kim: let's capture next steps here so we have alignment.
[08:13] Priya Sharma: action items: we'll share security pack, network diagrams, and sample infra code; Everguard to share CIDR map and region list.
[08:21] Maya Lopez: sounds good. one more question: do you have a recommended approach for service discovery in an internal microservice that calls Redwood - dns names, or service mesh integration?
[08:31] Priya Sharma: we support DNS names for the interface endpoint; integration with service meshes like Istio is possible by treating the endpoint as a standard upstream. we can give implementation notes.
[08:42] Ethan Ross: any SLA for Private deployments? we need 99.9 for production inference.
[08:48] Alex Kim: Dedicated customers can get SLA-backed uptime; Private deployments typically have an enterprise support add-on that includes uptime commitments. we'll include SLA options in the pricing doc.
[08:58] Samuel Price: can we do a quick run through of what you'll send in the security pack?
[09:02] Alex Kim: yes: SOC2 report, pen test summary, encryption architecture, KMS/HSM integration guide, network checklist, and an example contract addendum for data residency.
[09:13] Maya Lopez: perfect. let's plan the technical deep-dive with Priya and our infra folks next week or week after.
[09:20] Priya Sharma: happy to, i'll propose times for 2026-05-18/19.
[09:26] Alex Kim: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and proposed deep-dive. any final questions?
[09:30] Ethan Ross: none from infra, thanks.
[09:33] Samuel Price: all good.
[09:35] Maya Lopez: thanks, talk soon.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (company/product names sometimes misheard). References: will attach security pack (link to doc), sample terraform, and network diagram in follow-up email.

Recap (end): Alex to send security pack and SOC2 by 2026-05-10; Priya to share network diagram and infra snippets by 2026-05-12; Everguard to provide CIDR map by 2026-05-11; schedule technical deep-dive week of 2026-05-18.
